title: Nettle and the Kite Rescue
markdown:
The sun burst. Brilliant gold spilled across the meadow and painted the sleepy world. Birds piped a chatter-chatter song that tickled the air. Nettle the squirrel was still tucked snug in his drey, a cozy hollow in the tallest oak. A tiny twitch. A shivery shiver. The morning air felt different. It buzzed with something exciting. His whiskers tingled.

Then he remembered. His kite. His spectacular sky-blue kite with the long trailing rainbow tail. It had danced yesterday, a happy flutter against the blue. Until WHOOSH — a sudden gust, a tricky twist and turn, and POP. Stuck. Right at the tippy-top of the Big Apple Tree.

Nettle poked his nose out. The Big Apple Tree towered, impossibly tall, branches reaching like a giant’s tickly fingers. He shivered again. Too high. Definitely, absolutely too high for a little squirrel. His paws felt wobbly just thinking about it. He would never, ever get it down. A dreadful drop seemed to wait just out of sight.

BOOF. Biscuit the dog trotted up, tail thumping thunder on the dew. “Morning, Nettle. Ready for a fantastic day?”

Nettle pointed a shaky paw. “My kite. Stuck.”

Biscuit’s golden ears perked. He looked up, up, up. Eyes like saucers. “Sky-high perch. Don’t fret. We’ll fetch it together.”

“Together?” Nettle’s voice wobbled. “What if I fall?” He pictured a speck on a swaying branch. His heart flip-flopped.

“Together,” Biscuit said, tail a happy blur. “You scamper. I’ll boost.”

Nettle gulped. He tried. He really did. He scrambled a few feet up the rough bumpy bark. But a playful breeze tickled his ears and made the branches sway like a giant creaky swing. “Whoa.” He scrambled back down faster than a lightning flash. “Too much jiggle. Too much wobble. Funny tummy.” He buried his face in his paws. Too timid. Too high. The kite still winked from the tippy-top, as if it were waiting for a braver squirrel.

Biscuit sat, thought, then twinkled. “Nettle, Nettle, quick and keen. Better plan. I’ll help you climb and you can still be careful.”

“How, if I’m already scared?”

“I’ll bark brave. And at the tricky bit I’ll push this bouncy mushroom under you. Extra hop.” He nudged a spotted toadstool. It wobbled, delightful.

Nettle blinked. Peculiar. A bit fun. He missed the kite’s dance. He took a brave breath.

CAW. Mortimer the crow landed above the kite, beady and greedy. “Mine, mine.”

“Oh no.” Timid took a step back. The kite was in danger.

“Now, Nettle,” Biscuit boomed. “This is our moment.”

Something new flickered: not only fear. Determination. Nettle dashed up faster than he knew. “Bark, Biscuit. Give me your brave bark.”

“You’re a super-scamperer. A kite-capturer.”

A wide gap. He hesitated. Biscuit shoved the mushroom. Bounce, jiggle, up — enough to leap with a squeak of triumph.

Near the top the kite tangled in the finest leaves. Mortimer swooped. “Mine.”

“Not today.” Biscuit gave the trunk a mighty shake. RUMBLE. JIGGLE. Dust, rustle, talons scrape.

Nettle clung. The kite fluttered wild. One last tug of the shaking branches — the string loosened. Free.

He grabbed the rainbow tail, scrambled down sure-footed, and landed with a thump beside Biscuit, kite trailing like a captured cloud.

“We did it,” Nettle shouted, full of glee. He hugged Biscuit’s furry leg tightly. “We really, truly did it.”

Biscuit licked his nose, a warm wet kiss. “Told you. Together we can do anything.”

Nettle looked at the kite shimmering in the morning sun, then at his big loyal friend. The Big Apple Tree did not look like a giant anymore. The wind felt like a friendly whisper, not a scary push. They tore off across the gold grass, kite leaping behind, ready for whatever fantastic thing came next.

Together. The morning was still bursting, gold and chatter-chatter and a rainbow tail that had come home.
